text:
Ollie (People Ops): FYI thread 1 new hire Sofia Ramos currently working as a US-based contractor for us. Offer accepted to convert to FT on H-1B transfer. Questions: timeline for LCA posting, whether we should premium-file, payroll implications if start date is before transfer approval, and whether we cover any stamping costs if she travels abroad later. Proposed FT start: 2026-10-01.

Ken (Eng Manager): team needs her onboard early Oct ideally. We can be flexible a week or two.

Sofia Ramos: thanks all 1 couple specifics from my side: 1) I'm local in Bay Area now so I can do in-person I-9. 2) I'm open to premium processing if that helps. 3) If transfer is pending can I start as FT or do I stay on contractor pay?

Marco (Immigration Counsel): quick summary (non-legal): H-1B transfer workflow: employer files LCA (ETA-9035) then I-129 petition. Premium processing for H-1B transfers is available and shortens adjudication to ~15 calendar days. If you file a timely H-1B transfer and the candidate has lawful status, USCIS guidance allows employment to continue based on the receipt notice in many cases (but consult counsel for edge cases). For contractors converting to FT we recommend premium if business needs are time-sensitive. We will prepare LCA and job posting text.

Sana (Payroll): payroll note: contractor vs FT payroll are different systems. If Sofia's start date is set as FT 2026-10-01 but transfer finalizes later, we need a clear approval from Finance on retroactive pay/backpay and benefits eligibility. We prefer to onboard to US payroll only after transfer approval unless Finance signs off to start FT payroll upon I-129 receipt.

Lydia (Finance): we can consider retroactive FT pay for up to 2 pay periods upon transfer approval but need Sr. HR sign-off and justification. Benefits enrollment requires active FT payroll record; benefits effective dates may not be backdated. We'll confirm final decision after we see filing strategy.

Sofia Ramos: I'm fine to stay contractor until approval if that simplifies things, but prefer FT status sooner for benefits. Also any stamping later  will I need to travel? Not planning travel now.

Marco (Immigration Counsel): stamping only required if you leave the US and need a visa to re-enter. If Sofia remains in country and has valid admission, stamping isn't immediately necessary. Employer-covered stamping fees/courier: company policy typically reimburses visa-related travel and courier costs with receipts; premium filing fees are often paid by employer for sponsored hires (confirm with People Ops/Finance).

Ollie (People Ops): policy: Redwood covers USCIS filing & premium fees for hires at IC2+ (subject to Finance approval). We reimburse reasonable travel and courier expenses with receipts. Will confirm Sofia's IC level and loop Finance.

Ken (Eng Manager): confirm IC2  ok to cover filing. We want premium if it shortens risk.

Marco (Immigration Counsel): suggested plan: 1) Ollie -> approve IC level + confirm premium fee coverage with Lydia. 2) People Ops to send role description for LCA. 3) Marco to draft LCA and job posting text (10 business day notice posting can start immediately). 4) Sofia to upload contractor docs and passport copy for file. 5) Decide premium vs regular filing.

Sofia Ramos: I'll DM passport scan and contractor agreement today. Will stay on contractor pay if needed.

Sana (Payroll): reminder: for I-9 we need Section 1 completed on or before first day of employment; Section 2 can be completed in person if Sofia is physically in US (she said she is). If we transition from contractor to FT same week, bring a copy of contractor agreement and new FT offer to onboarding.

Lydia (Finance): action: pending Ollie confirmation, Finance tentatively approves employer payment of I-129 + premium. Please include cost center. Also: if payroll retroactive approval requested, submit justification and expected backpay amount before FT onboarding.

Marco (Immigration Counsel): filing note: LCA processing is ~7 business days; we post notice for 10 business days to comply with internal rules (we don't need third-party posting but keep the record). Premium filing shortens adjudication but does not change LCA timeline.

Ollie (People Ops): action items: - Ollie to confirm IC level and reply here (owner: Ollie) - Marco to prepare LCA draft and post notice (owner: Marco) - Sofia to DM passport & contractor docs (owner: Sofia) - Lydia/Finance to confirm premium fee approval and cost center (owner: Lydia) - Ken to hold FT start window 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-08 (owner: Ken)

Sofia Ramos: DMed passport and contract. Thanks.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: upload signed FT offer to `/onboarding/docs` and book I-9 verifier slot for first day.

Sana (Payroll): once we have final approval, I'll send the FT onboarding packet and benefits snapshot. If Sofia stays contractor for an interim week please ensure contractor invoice submitted to `/expenses` so payment continues.

Ken (Eng Manager): we'll plan for Sofia to start sprint work 2026-10-01 if transfer clears. If not, she can join as contractor for a week.

Ollie (People Ops): closing note: will circle back with confirmed premium approval and post LCA by EOD tomorrow. Please keep updates here.
